did_you_know.text: The story takes place in the days when the judges ruled, a time when there was a famine in the land. Because of the famine, a man from Bethlehem in Judah leaves with his wife and two sons and moves to the fields of Moab.
The family members are Elimelech, Naomi, Mahlon, and Chilion. The text calls them Ephrathites and notes that they were from Bethlehem in Judah.
Mahlon and Chilion marry Moabite women: one is named Orpah and the other Ruth. The family lives in the fields of Moab for about ten years.
After Elimelech dies, Mahlon and Chilion also die. Naomi is left without her husband and her two sons.
Naomi decides to return from Moab to Judah after hearing that the LORD had come to the aid of his people and given them food.
Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to return to their mothers’ homes and wishes that the LORD will show them the same kindness they showed to the dead and to her.
Naomi explains to her daughters-in-law that she has no more sons for them to marry, so she asks them to return and continue with their lives.
Orpah says goodbye to Naomi and returns to her people, while Ruth clings to Naomi. In this way, the text highlights the difference between the choices of the two daughters-in-law.
Ruth declares her loyalty to Naomi: she is willing to go wherever Naomi goes, live among her people, and worship her God.
Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. This indicates when they arrived and that food would soon be available.
